long_biography.plain_text:
As a university physics student in the mid-1970s, David Anders McIntyre cut grass for extra money while Dutch elm disease stripped mature trees from Midwestern streets. He experimented with treatments, reinvested early earnings in a truck and equipment, and named his fledgling business Ceres after the Roman goddess of agriculture. The tree-care operation became the foundation of Ceres Environmental Services.

McIntyre shifted the business toward large-scale recovery and civil works, personally overseeing hundreds of federally reimbursed projects after hurricanes, wildfires, tornadoes and other disasters. Its assignments have ranged from debris removal and demolition to recycling, coastal recovery and infrastructure rebuilding. After the Christchurch earthquakes, he extended Ceres into New Zealand for demolition and reconstruction work. In 2012, the group bought the damaged Peterborough Apartments with the stated intention of restoring the heritage building rather than demolishing it.

As a university physics student in the mid-1970s, David Anders McIntyre cut grass for extra money while Dutch elm disease stripped mature trees from Midwestern streets. The tree-care operation became the foundation of Ceres Environmental Services.

McIntyre shifted the business toward large-scale recovery and civil works, personally overseeing hundreds of federally reimbursed projects after hurricanes, wildfires, tornadoes and other disasters. Its assignments have ranged from debris removal and demolition to recycling, coastal recovery and infrastructure rebuilding.
